_about: PROTOTYPE FIXTURE. Evidence reviewed 2026-10-29 from production (read-only app_projects rows) and the Ecology SEPA documents fetched for JODY video 3006. Grades: a = official direct. The person named as applicant in the MDNS is not shown.

defining_record.label: Washington Department of Ecology SEPA register, record 202603632

summary: A six-story building with 98 apartments and 1,932 square feet of retail, at the corner of N 26th Street and N Madison Street in Tacoma.
It replaces a vacant former bank building. The City of Tacoma found no significant environmental impacts, on one condition: soil testing before demolition.

latest.title: Shoring permits filed with the City of Tacoma
latest.body: A site development permit (SDEV26-0272) and a building permit for retaining walls (BLDCA26-0284). Tacoma's permit system shows the retaining-wall permit as Ready to Issue and the site permit as needing a pre-construction meeting.
latest.changes_status: Does not change the project's lifecycle. These permits cover shoring, not the building.
latest.observed: Statuses as read from Tacoma's permit data on Oct 29, 2026.

next.text: The comment period on the city's environmental determination closed Sept 10, 2026. The city says appeals go to Pierce County Superior Court within 21 days after the building permit is issued.
next.scope: No permit for the main building appears in the Tacoma permit records we track.

opportunity.title: Public comment on the environmental determination

known: The city issued a Mitigated Determination of Non-Significance (LU25-0180) on Aug 27, 2026.
The project is a permitted use in its zone and needs no discretionary land use permit.
The site is inside the former Asarco smelter plume. The city requires soil testing before demolition.
A demolition permit (DEMOC26-0014) shows Permit Issued in Tacoma's permit system.
unknown: When the demolition permit was issued. JODY's records show its status, not the date.
Who owns the land. It is not stated in the documents reviewed.
The site plan, Phase I environmental assessment and soil management plan. They are listed but not read.
Whether the city's MDNS calls the site "undeveloped" by mistake; the checklist and traffic study describe a paved former bank.

impacts.text: The traffic study expects 675 weekday trips, 34 in the morning peak hour and 54 in the evening peak hour, and concludes no significant impact.
Arsenic in the 40 to 100 ppm range is mapped for the site, and an old diesel tank was closed in place in 1996.
98 apartments, about 20% designated for low income, and 0.68 parking stalls per unit.

timeline.title: Department of Ecology comments on the proposal
timeline.body: Asks that hazardous materials in the old building be handled before demolition, and notes a contaminated site within a quarter mile.
